title: The seawall, no grid
logline: The seawall drawn straight across the page where three gutters would have been. Nothing interrupts it. The first page the eye reads as one thing.

panels.composition: The seawall's long curve across the full width of the page, uninterrupted, the bay above it, main street's backs below it, the places where a Sunday's gutters would have fallen marked by nothing at all. A crow on the wall. Wet January light.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a long concrete seawall curving across the entire width of a page with a bay above and the backs of a small town below, a crow on the wall, nothing interrupting the line, no words

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards
